I am relatively new to learning Japanese and have been using wanikani for the past few weeks. I absolutely love it, but I just finished up level 2 and I am hoping there might be some free alternatives out there. I have been searching the past few days but haven't really had any luck. The kanjidamage anki decks are alright, but not as polished and it doesn't work as well with having scheduled reviews in my opinion. I would appreciate any alternative suggestions or good anki decks. Also, how should I be using anki? I feel like I'm using the program incorrectly.
Free alternatives to wanikani for learning kanji and vocab?
I took some Japanese language courses at my local community college. We used a textbook called Genki. Their online self-study resources are pretty good.

I've been using kanjidamage.com in combination with a "kanji damage" course on memrise. It's been pretty useful so far. The course sometimes uses slightly different translations to the kanji damage ones; but as you learn your vocab you quickly learn which of the interpretations is the more accurate.

In the last 3-4 months I've covered about 1070 kanji/radicals and can still remember a good 95% of them. The last 5% gets brushed up pretty regularly through memrise if I keep forgetting them. Provided you at least review everything once a day. (got an 85 day streak so far)

Thank you for mentioning this! Funny you mention that website, I just started using it last night. I find it very helpful and motivational to have a streak system. I had no idea there was a kanjidamage course on there though, that's going to be really helpful.

No problem, man. Here's the link if you're looking for it: http://www.memrise.com/course/15879/kanji-damage-full-course/

The guy who made the memrise course also made a sister one you can do after you've finished kanjidamage that has the rest of the kanji required for JLPT N1 but aren't covered by kanjidamage.

There's a very small amount of kanji where the font didn't have the radical alone or it shows slightly differently (I think the memrise font in the web-browser is Chinese). But they're very few and far between, so you can probably brute-force remember those ones. I've encountered like less than 10 of those in the 1,000+ I've gone through.

I've been adding the kanji damage mnemonics to the mems for each kanji when someone else hasn't already or there isn't a better (I think) alternative mnemonic. So if you don't overshoot me in terms of progress there should be plenty of mnemonics there for remembering.

Oh yeah. You'll probably want to ignore the pronunciation sections as you get up to them.

Memrise isn't really designed for that sort of thing so you can often get every single possible pronunciation for a kanji and have them all correct. But it marks you down because it wanted them in a different order.

I've actually found that as I learn vocab I start to pair words up with the kanji I know as I go along anyway. The pronunciations are kinda meaningless if you don't already know the words they're part of.
